title: Needlepoint session trail mapper: compact correlated-span navigator
creator: Alex Kim
description: Design a compact, scannable session-trail mapper for the Redwood Console's tracing view that helps engineers quickly identify causal spans across services, surface cost and latency signals at the span level, and highlight sessions associated with active rollouts/canaries. This ticket covers a high-fidelity prototype, interaction spec, and a short usability walkthrough for SRE and platform engineers.
goals: Enable rapid identification of the most expensive/slow spans in a request session
Surface correlation breadcrumbs to jump between related sessions (same correlation-id across services)
Integrate rollout metadata: mark sessions that belong to canary/experiment cohorts and allow filtering by rollout state
Keep the main trace canvas compact for wide screens and embed a mini 'session trail' strip for quick scanning
acceptance_criteria: Prototype shows a compact lane view (service lanes) with collapse/expand and per-span cost sparkline
Hover card exists showing span metadata: service, op name, tokens, estimated cost, latency, model variant, correlation-id link
Filter controls implemented in prototype: latency > X, cost > $Y, rollout==canary, model==redwood-v1
Link-out to full request detail and to related sessions with same correlation-id
Design review feedback from Eng and PM addressed and recorded
design_notes: We intentionally keep the default canvas density low: show only root + 2 child depth on initial load with an affordance to expand deeper. Cost is estimated from token counts and execution tier; use subtle color-scale rather than numeric first to avoid noise. Rollout markers are small pill chips on session rows; hovering shows rollout name + percentage. Correlation breadcrumb trail appears above the canvas as a horizontally scrollable pill bar. The mini-map on the right is interactive for quick scrub and snap-to-span.
decisions: Use a two-tier visual emphasis: color hue for latency bucket and width for cost magnitude
Hovercards should include a 'Jump to session' action linking to a session-by-id route rather than opening a modal to maintain context
Do not show raw token counts by default; show estimated cost and provide option in details panel to toggle raw tokens
Combine correlation-id search with dynamic suggestion of recent matching sessions in the pill bar
engineering_notes: Prototype includes annotated CSS specs for lane collapse animation and a suggested data payload shape for the hovercard (flat list of span entries with precomputed cost/latency buckets). Eng pointed out we need a backend endpoint to fetch correlated sessions by correlation-id with pagination. Also flagged potential performance hit for sessions with >2000 spans—prototype suggests lazy-loading deeper spans as separate requests.
open_questions: Should the rollout chip be tappable on mobile or only show on hover on desktop?
Do we expose quantization/model variant at the span level or aggregate at the session level?
What is the canonical cost unit for display across Console (USD vs credits)?
implementation_plan: 1) Finalize hovercard fields and sample payload with ENG. 2) Hand off Figma frames + interaction spec (micro-interactions) to Eng for a small spike. 3) Run a short usability test with 6 internal engineers and collect task completion metrics (find highest-latency span, filter to canary sessions, follow correlation chain). 4) Iterate and prepare for console-2025.02 release.
